clue.text: Boat's the same even when capsized

indicators.note: a craft that stays the same when turned over is a word reading identically backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A small craft is said to look no different after rolling over in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capsized' suggests a boat overturning; here it means the word read backwards, which gives the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A kayak is a small, light canoe-like craft paddled by one person.

clue.text: Device for making bits smaller, or larger, we hear

indicators.note: the phrase signals that the word for larger is to be spoken, not written

parts.note: larger means greater

explanation.surface: A kitchen tool is described, with a quibble about whether it shrinks or enlarges things.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen shredder reduces cheese or vegetables to small pieces by rubbing them on a rough surface.

clue.text: Nuts go well with cheese

definitions.meaning: dry savoury biscuits are served with a cheeseboard

explanation.surface: A snack suggestion: nuts make a good pairing with cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for mad, and also the plural of a dry biscuit eaten with cheese.

clue.text: Values seem set for a change

indicators.note: the letters are set out differently, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's principles appear about to shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' rearranges SEEMSET into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To value someone is to hold them in high regard, a verb in the third person singular.

clue.text: A length boxers go to to avoid KO?

definitions.meaning: a length is a span or interval of space

definitions.text: boxers go to to avoid KO?
definitions.meaning: a boxer who lasts all the scheduled rounds without being knocked out is said to go this far

explanation.surface: A question about how far a fighter must last in the ring to escape being knocked out.
explanation.definitionFit: A span of space between two points, and the full number of rounds in the idiom 'go the ...'.

clue.text: Mabel gets entangled with chap in US resort

indicators.note: the letters get tangled together and so are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman called Mabel becomes romantically involved with a man while on holiday in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets entangled' mixes the letters of MABEL and CHAP together.
explanation.definitionFit: A wealthy coastal town in Florida, a well-known American holiday destination.

clue.text: It may make one smart, top or bottom

definitions.text: It may make one smart, top or bottom

parts.words: It may make one smart, top or bottom
parts.note: used on the head it tidies one up; applied to the backside as a spanking it makes one sting

explanation.surface: Something that can make a person look neat or feel pain, depending on where it is used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' has two senses: neat (for the head) and sting (for the bottom, after a spanking with the back of the brush).
explanation.definitionFit: A grooming tool for the head whose flat back was once used to smack children.

clue.text: Clergyman wants caviar, not a pie

indicators.note: printer's pie is a jumble of type, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A churchman turns down the pastry and asks for fish roe instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a' takes one A out of CAVIAR; 'pie' (printer's pie, jumbled type) rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish priest in the Church of England is a member of the clergy.

clue.text: Not the sole order dogs learn to obey

definitions.meaning: the back part of the foot or shoe, as opposed to the underside
a command telling a dog to walk close beside its owner

explanation.surface: A remark about obedience training: this is not the only command a dog is taught.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear part of a shoe or foot, and the command bringing a dog to walk at one's side.

clue.text: Quietly object to a small portion

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly
an object is an article, a thing

explanation.surface: Someone softly protests at being served too little food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'object' looks like a verb (protest) but is the noun, a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny piece or fragment of something is a minute part of it.

clue.text: Bury someone because of the wrong note given to the doctor?

indicators.note: the letters of the word are set down wrongly, so they are rearranged

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Someone is buried after a doctor receives a mistaken message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges NOTE into ENTO; MB follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To place a body in a tomb or grave is to inter it.

clue.text: At liberty to be generous

definitions.meaning: at liberty means not imprisoned, loose

explanation.surface: Someone is permitted to be open-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: Not confined, and also liberal or lavish, as in giving freely.

clue.text: Stay well away from work

parts.note: reads as keeping a good distance from the job, but describes remaining healthy while feigning illness to skip it

explanation.surface: Advice to keep a good distance from the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' looks like 'far', but means 'healthy': staying healthy while absent is shamming sickness.
explanation.definitionFit: To pretend illness so as to avoid duty or work is to shirk.

clue.text: He's given unwarranted responsibility

parts.note: sounds like an undeserved promotion, but describes someone wrongly blamed for others' faults

explanation.surface: A man is handed a job he has not earned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'responsibility' suggests a duty or post; it means blame.
explanation.definitionFit: A person made to carry the blame for others' wrongdoing, from the biblical goat sent into the wilderness.

clue.text: He makes a practice of seeing complaints

definitions.text: He makes a practice of seeing complaints

parts.words: He makes a practice of seeing complaints
parts.note: sounds like a complaints officer, but describes a medical man whose practice deals with eye disorders

explanation.surface: A man whose habit is to hear grievances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seeing complaints' means disorders of sight, and 'practice' is a medical practice.
explanation.definitionFit: An old term for an eye doctor, one who treats diseases of vision.

clue.text: A sticky sweet

parts.note: read as a gummy confection, but the sweet is one on a stick

explanation.surface: A gooey piece of confectionery.
explanation.definitionFit: A boiled confection mounted on a small stick and licked.

clue.text: The attendant's not responsible for it

definitions.text: The attendant's not responsible for it

parts.words: The attendant's not responsible for it
parts.note: sounds like a staff member denying blame, but someone in attendance cannot be the cause of not being there

explanation.surface: A steward disclaims responsibility for some mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attendant' means one who attends, is present, the opposite of being away.
explanation.definitionFit: Being away or not present, the state that someone who attends avoids.

clue.text: Private quarters

parts.note: sounds like a secluded room, but means lodgings for soldiers of the lowest rank

explanation.surface: Rooms closed to the public.
explanation.definitionFit: Buildings housing soldiers, the living quarters of privates.

clue.text: He leaves his country to be protected by another

definitions.text: He leaves his country to be protected by another

parts.words: He leaves his country to be protected by another
parts.note: a straightforward description of someone fleeing abroad for asylum

explanation.surface: A man flees his homeland for the safety of another nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who flees persecution or war at home and seeks asylum abroad.

clue.text: Sweet disorder in the bed

definitions.meaning: a prank bed with sheets folded so the sleeper cannot stretch out is named after this dessert

explanation.surface: A pleasant untidiness among the bedclothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit pudding in pastry, and the 'apple-pie bed', a practical joke with folded sheets.

clue.text: Quiet time for a hotel employee

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical direction for quiet
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A peaceful moment for someone working in a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: A uniformed boy who runs errands in a hotel, a bellboy.

clue.text: They marked the passing of the horse-drawn vehicle

definitions.text: They marked the passing of the horse-drawn vehicle

parts.words: They marked the passing of the horse-drawn vehicle
parts.note: sounds like mourners noting the end of the carriage era, but describes grooves left on a road by wheels

explanation.surface: People commemorated the end of horse-drawn transport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marked the passing' suggests mourning; it means literally left marks as the cart passed.
explanation.definitionFit: Grooves worn in a track by repeated wheels.

clue.text: It doesn't describe the present schoolboy

definitions.text: It doesn't describe the present schoolboy

parts.words: It doesn't describe the present schoolboy
parts.note: sounds like a word for the modern pupil, but means one who is not present in class

explanation.surface: A word said to be out of date for today's pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil who stays away from school without permission.

clue.text: Threatened strike that doesn't come off

definitions.text: Threatened strike that doesn't come off

parts.words: Threatened strike that doesn't come off
parts.note: sounds like a called-off industrial action, but describes a sham blow in fencing or boxing

explanation.surface: Workers threaten a walkout that never happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests industrial action; it is a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretended attack or blow meant to deceive an opponent.

clue.text: An egg I scrambled, obviously not new-laid

indicators.note: scrambled means the letters are jumbled, apt with eggs

explanation.surface: Someone scrambles an egg that is clearly far from fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: Growing older, the reverse of freshly produced.

clue.text: Girl thought to be like Queen Victoria

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
mused means thought, pondered

explanation.surface: A young woman reckoned to resemble the old monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Victoria is famously quoted as saying 'We are not amused'.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Victoria's supposed remark makes her the model of someone not entertained.

clue.text: Time to settle final accounts?

parts.note: sounds like an accountant's year-end deadline, but describes the Last Judgement when all sins are reckoned up

explanation.surface: A question about when the last bills fall due.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accounts' suggests bookkeeping; the moment meant is judgement for one's deeds.
explanation.definitionFit: The Last Judgement, or any moment when one must answer for past actions.

clue.text: See 27
